title: Linux CLI and Bash Basics
summary: Practice small shell scripts in controlled temporary workspaces.

modules.title: Shell Output
modules.summary: Use Bash commands to write predictable output.

lessons.title: Echo A Status
lessons.concept_md: `echo` writes text to standard output. Shell scripts become useful when each command has a clear observable result.

lessons.title: Use A Shell Variable
lessons.concept_md: Shell variables store text for later commands. Double quotes keep the variable expansion readable and predictable.
lessons.prompt: Update the script so it prints `hello padawan`.
lessons.hidden_hint: Only the value assigned to `name` needs to change.

lessons.title: Write A File
lessons.concept_md: Redirection sends command output to a file. `>` replaces a file, while `>>` appends to it.
lessons.prompt: Create a file named `status.txt` that contains `green`.
lessons.hidden_hint: Keep the filename, change the value being redirected.

lessons.title: Check A Condition
lessons.concept_md: Shell scripts often check files before deciding what to do next. `grep -q` tests for matching text without printing it.
lessons.prompt: Update the script so it prints `deploy` when `status.txt` contains `green`.
lessons.starter_code:
echo green > status.txt
if grep -q green status.txt; then
  echo waiting
fi
lessons.hidden_hint: The condition is already correct; change the command inside the `then` block.
